newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines tells rice traders not to hike prices.
newsitem.headline: Philippines tells rice traders not to hike prices.

text.p: The Philippine government on Tuesday told rice traders not to raise prices following last week's de facto peso devaluation and said it had enough stocks to swamp the market if necessary.

"The NFA (National Food Authority) has more than enough stocks in its warehouses and it is ready to flood the market with affordable rice should some unscrupulous traders resort to hoarding to fuel any price rises," NFA Administrator Joemari Gerochi said in a statement.
He insisted that prices would not change.
At present, regular milled rice are being sold at 14 pesos a kg and well-milled rice at 15 pesos. Both prices were set last year.
The peso has slumped around 11 percent since last Friday's effective devaluation and inflation is certain to rise as a result.
The Philippines imports only about six percent of its rice needs. It expects to produce 11 million tonnes this year.
Current commercial and household stocks are estimated to be at two million tonnes.
An NFA official said they had not seen any sign of hoarding but were making daily checks on prices of the food staple.
The NFA gave a phone number for the public to call if they spot any unauthorised price increase.
